studies.label: Development and preliminary content testing of the EQ-5D-Y-5L
studies.family_rationale: The principal contribution was new EQ-5D-Y content with five severity levels. Label generation, target-group testing, revision, and cross-language harmonization produced the EQ-5D-Y-5L instrument version.

items.statement: Cross-language comparison found some divergent wording, but the harmonization exercise judged the language-specific severity labels comparable and retained the labels developed by the national teams.
The study produced a self-report EQ-5D-Y-5L with five severity levels in each of five dimensions, defining 3125 possible health states.
The authors concluded that the study successfully established a comprehensible and feasible five-level EQ-5D-Y version for children and adolescents aged 8–15 years.
The authors stated that the study was the first, to their knowledge, to demonstrate the feasibility of response scaling tasks in participants as young as eight years.
The authors stated that psychometric testing, comparison with EQ-5D-Y-3L, and examination of feasibility in health-state valuation are required before extensive use.
Convenience samples were used in all countries and both study phases, so the study populations were not representative of the national populations.

Children and adolescents with a health condition were difficult to recruit. In UK Phase 2, the researchers recruited schoolchildren only because recruitment of children with current experience of illness would have required separate NHS ethical approval and caused a substantial delay.

items.exact_state: The study produced a self-report version of the EQ-5D-Y-5L with German, Spanish, Swedish, and UK English language-specific content.

items.label: Cross-language comparability of severity labels
items.description: Language-specific labels need not be literal equivalents when target-group evidence supports locally natural wording, but their positions on the severity continuum should remain comparable.

items.label: Continuity of health-status measurement across childhood and adulthood
items.description: The five-level youth format maintains structural comparability with the adult EQ-5D-5L and could support health-status measurement over the life course.
